claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
A 5–10 μm Al2O3 coating is the proposed intervention.
Applying an Al2O3 coating to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
The Al2O3 coating will preserve the alloy's useful mechanical performance.
The proposed coating produces or constitutes a protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Preventing oxygen diffusion reduces oxidation and improves resistance to high-temperature corrosion.
The prediction applies to exposure in air at 1000 °C for 100 hours.
The proposed mechanical-loading boundary is stress below 500 MPa.
After coating and exposure, the alloy will maintain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
After coating and exposure, the alloy will maintain room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Coated specimens will be compared with untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr specimens after high-temperature air exposure.
The experiment will measure oxygen diffusion rate, yield strength, tensile ductility, and coating thickness and integrity.

contradictions.description: The loading boundary restricts stress to below 500 MPa, while the predicted retained yield-strength range extends to 530 MPa. The hypothesis does not explain how the upper end of that range would be measured or validated under the stated boundary.
